findings.claim: Repo.Validate's namePattern (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`) accepts the literal names "." and ".." for a repo's Name field — the field the file's own package doc calls 'the concept security boundary' (request input only ever selects a repo by Name) and whose field comment states 'the name is also the repo's mining folder under sessions/'. Nothing in Validate (lines 35-58) rejects a dot-only Name, unlike the parallel traversal guard in internal/sessions/sessions.go's validateScopeName (same file set, same review) which explicitly excludes "." and ".." (`name == "." || name == ".."`) for the identical concern — a scope name becoming a path segment under the sessions store. Registering a repo via the add-repo endpoint (internal/server/repos.go — cross-chunk, confirmed caller: filepath grep shows repos.go is the only HTTP-reachable constructor of a Repo{} before Validate) with Name=".." passes validation; any later code that builds `filepath.Join(sessionsDir, repo.Name, ...)` for that repo's mining folder (per registry.go's own comment) resolves one directory above the intended sessions root — a path-traversal primitive reachable from the one place the package promises request input is constrained to a safe Name.
findings.fix: In Repo.Validate (internal/repos/registry.go), reject Name == "." and Name == ".." explicitly (mirroring sessions.validateScopeName), e.g. `if r.Name == "." || r.Name == ".." { return fmt.Errorf(...) }` before or alongside the reserved-name check.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/repos/registry.go lines 1-58 in full: the package doc (line 1-4) states 'Repo paths come exclusively from the registry file — request input only ever selects by name (concept security boundary)'; Validate (lines 35-58) checks Label length, Name against namePattern, the two reserved names 'default'/'archived', and that Path is absolute — it has no check excluding '.' or '..', both of which match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`. Re-read internal/sessions/sessions.go lines 221-230: validateScopeName explicitly lists `name == "." || name == ".."` as unsafe for the same category of path-segment risk. Re-read registry_test.go's TestRegistryAdd (lines 53-114): no test case exercises Name="." or Name="..", confirming the gap is untested. Confirmed the only Repo{}-constructing HTTP path is internal/server/repos.go via a targeted grep (cross-chunk file, not re-read in full per chunk-scope rule); the downstream sessions-folder join itself lives in that cross-chunk file and was not re-read line-by-line — flagged as a cross-chunk dependency in notes accordingly, which is why exposure is scored 'rare' rather than 'often' and effect kept at 'incorrect' rather than 'destructive'.

notes: Cross-chunk suspicion (not chased): internal/repos/registry.go's package doc says a repo's Name becomes 'the repo's mining folder under sessions/', but the actual filepath.Join that uses repo.Name to build that folder path lives in internal/server (sessions.go/repos.go), outside this chunk's manifest. That file also owns the only HTTP-reachable Repo{} constructor (handleReposAdd-style handler in internal/server/repos.go) confirmed via grep. Recommend the server/go-core chunk (or whichever lane covers internal/server) verify whether repo.Name is joined into a sessions-dir path unguarded, which would raise security-MAJ-1 (internal/repos/registry.go) to destructive/often. No other cross-chunk dependency found for the remaining 32 files — contextdocs.ChooseFolder's prompt argument was checked via grep against its two internal/server callers (config_items.go:45, repos.go:635) and both pass a fixed string literal, so the Go-%q-into-PowerShell-string pattern in internal/contextdocs/sync.go's chooseFolderWindows is not currently reachable with attacker-controlled input — not filed as a finding, but worth a NIT-level note for whoever reviews internal/contextdocs/sync.go: that quoting mismatch is a latent injection primitive if any future caller ever passes a non-literal prompt. windows-only files (cmd/configserver/install_windows.go, internal/routines/sched_windows.go) build PowerShell command strings with fmt.Sprintf around a routine Label / serverTaskName; Label is constrained by Scan() to the plist's own filename (repo-controlled, not reachable via Duplicate's namePattern-validated newName, which itself excludes quote characters), so no injection path found in this chunk.
